extracted.intended_audience: early-stage startup founders and startup PR/marketing leads
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for announcing early-stage startup news and pitching reporters, focused on seed-stage companies and founder-led PR. Advice emphasizes longevity, honesty, reporter relationships, and investor-facing message quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will this story exist in Google search 2 years from now?
rubrics_metrics.description: Will this story exist in Google search 2 years from now in a way that helps us?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a pre-pitch filter: prefer announcements that create long-term discoverability and value (SEO/longevity). If it won't be useful long-term, reconsider pitching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness if competitor copies the announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a competitor copies the announcement next week, will we still look distinct?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure framing and facts are specific enough that competitors can't easily appropriate the story and make you indistinguishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't mistake press for validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders mistake 'press' for 'validation'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating media coverage as a substitute for real traction or product-market fit; reporters are not investors or customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding announcements must say something useful
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding announcements that say nothing useful
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements should communicate substantive information beyond dollar amount—what you build and how the funding will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't use customer logos without quotes or context
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer logos used without quotes or context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cite customers, provide verifiable context or quotes rather than relying on logos alone as proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unverifiable 'first in our category' claims
rubrics_metrics.description: 'First in our category' claims that aren't verifiable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from grandiose category-first claims unless you can substantiate them with clear, verifiable criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't rely on anonymous beta testers as sole proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymous beta testers as the only proof
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide identifiable, verifiable evidence of user/customer adoption rather than anonymous or unsubstantiated testers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Would your competitors say this about you? Would your customers say this about you? Would your engineers cringe at this claim? If yes to any: rewrite
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run claims through these three checks and rewrite any messaging that fails; ensures internal consistency and external verifiability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skip wire releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Skip wire releases entirely
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For seed-stage announcements, avoid generic wire services and focus on targeted outreach and owned channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build 1:1 relationships with reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Build 1:1 with 5 reporters who cover your space
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to develop direct relationships with a small set of relevant beat reporters rather than mass blasting PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a useful source on adjacent industry stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Become a useful source on industry stories you're NOT in
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer reporter value on broader stories to earn credibility and future coverage, even for areas where you're not the primary subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earn coverage by being quoted in others' stories first
rubrics_metrics.description: Earn coverage by being quoted in others' stories first
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position founders/team as expert sources to accumulate quoted authority that leads to profile pieces later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish long-tail blog post on your own site for SEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-tail blog post on your own site for SEO
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use owned content to capture long-tail search traffic and ensure your message exists on a permanent, indexable page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder must come across as substantive
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the founder come across as substantive?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investors and reporters look for founders who sound thoughtful and knowledgeable rather than superficial or performative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics should be specific, not hand-wavy
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the metrics specific or hand-wavy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concrete metrics and context (growth rates, conversion, usage) over vague or vanity numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing must show real differentiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there real differentiation in the framing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate a unique angle that competitors cannot easily claim; avoid generic positioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company should know its market
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the company seem to know its market?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate market understanding in press messaging—customer segments, problems solved, and competitive landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with what you're building, not the dollar amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead with what you're building, not the dollar amount
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make product, mission, and traction the headline; funding size should be secondary contextual information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name specific use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Name specific use of funds (engineers in X, expansion to Y)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain concrete allocations so readers (and investors) understand how the money will change the business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote a lead investor with substantive reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote a lead investor with substantive reasoning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an investor quote that adds insight into why the company is compelling, not a generic endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague boilerplate growth language
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'to fuel growth' and 'to accelerate' language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace clichés with specific explanations of goals and mechanisms; vague phrases signal low substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: If mentioning dollar amount, explain runway
rubrics_metrics.description: If you must mention dollar amount, say what runway it gives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate funding into operational terms (e.g., months of runway, hires enabled) so the number has meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder tone: smart and humble
rubrics_metrics.description: Founder presents as smart and humble
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a balance of competence and humility in quotes and messaging; arrogance or overclaiming undermines credibility.
